title: From Sparse Dependence to Sparse Attention: Unveiling How Chain-of-Thought Enhances Transformer Sample Efficiency

contributions.purpose: Explain why Chain-of-Thought (CoT) helps LLMs even when expressiveness is not the limiting factor, by studying it from a sample-efficiency rather than an expressiveness perspective.
contributions.mechanism: Theoretical training-dynamics analysis on a parity-learning testbed with a simplified transformer: prove parity is representable by a 1-layer transformer, then bound sample complexity with vs. without CoT.
contributions.evaluation: Theorems 1-3: without CoT, learning parity needs exponentially many samples under limited parameters; with CoT data (sparse sequential dependence) a 1-layer transformer learns parity with almost linear samples w.r.t. sequence length.
contributions.source_quote: Theoretically, we show that while the parity problem can be expressed by a 1-layer transformer, learning requires exponentially many samples without CoT when the number of parameters is limited (Theorem 1 and 2). Meanwhile, for CoT data with sparse sequential dependence, a 1-layer transformer can learn the parity function and faithfully represent the sparse dependence in its attention pattern with almost linear samples with respect to sequence length (Theorem 3).

contributions.purpose: Identify the mechanism by which CoT improves learning, and validate that it holds beyond synthetic settings.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical measurement of attention sparsity via normalized attention entropy, training/evaluating with and without CoT on synthetic parity data and on real pretrained LMs.
contributions.evaluation: Training on parity with CoT needs only polynomial samples and induces sparse, interpretable attention (Figure 3); evaluating and training on CoT data also induces sparser attention on the real-world GSM-8k dataset with pretrained language models.
contributions.source_quote: Empirically, we verify our analysis that training on parity function with CoT data requires only polynomial samples and will induce sparse and interpretable attention (Figure 3). We further show that evaluating and training on CoT data will also induce sparser attention on real-world dataset GSM-8k on pretrained language models.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Recent theoretical studies suggest that CoT enhances a model's expressiveness, increasing its representational capacity when the sequence is long enough Feng et al. (2023); Li et al. (2024c). However, expressivity alone does not guarantee success.
To conduct the theoretical analysis, we simplify the Transformer architecture similar to prior works (see e.g. Wang et al. (2024b); Nichani et al. (2024); Li et al. (2023b)).

notes: Theory-first paper; core claim reframes CoT's benefit from expressiveness to sample efficiency via induced attention sparsity. No negative/tie results reported; results are consistently favorable to the CoT-sparsity hypothesis. Real-world evidence limited to attention-sparsity trends on GSM-8k (correlational), not full end-to-end accuracy gains.
